sentenceSets.sentence: The committee's otiose proceedings continued for months, producing recommendations that no one had the authority or intention to implement.

answerChoices.reasoning: The sentence does say the proceedings ran for months, which makes length a tempting reading, but length alone would not explain why the recommendations went nowhere; the clause about no one having authority or intention points to work that could never matter, not merely work that took a long time.

Desultory work jumps around without method, yet the sentence describes proceedings that continued steadily for months and actually produced recommendations at the end, so the problem is not a lack of follow-through but the emptiness of the result.
A perfunctory effort is done quickly and without care, which contradicts proceedings sustained over months; the sentence faults the outcome, not the amount of attention the committee gave the task.
Something moribund is dying out, but these proceedings kept going and delivered a product, so the sentence describes activity that accomplished nothing rather than activity that was winding down.
Nothing in the sentence describes disagreement or bad feeling among the members; the only failure named is that no one would act on what they wrote.
Proceedings that generate formal recommendations for other parties to implement are not being kept secret, and the sentence raises no question of concealment.

Months of meetings might suggest thoroughness, but the sentence points at how little the output could ever accomplish, and a thorough inquiry would not be described by the clause about no one intending to act.
An improvised process is unplanned, whereas the sentence shows a committee following a course long enough to arrive at written recommendations.
The sentence ends by noting that nothing would be implemented, which is the opposite of a process that settles anything.
Recommendations that no one has the authority or intention to carry out are by definition without consequence in the sentence's own terms.
No money, payment, or gain appears anywhere in the sentence, which concerns only whether the committee's output would be acted on.

sentenceSets.sentence: During the cleanup the engineer deleted several otiose lines of code that had been copied forward through a dozen revisions without ever executing.

answerChoices.reasoning: Redundancy requires that something else already does the same job, but the sentence says these lines never executed at all, so they were not duplicating work performed elsewhere.
Calling the lines obsolete implies they once did useful work and were later superseded, while the sentence says they never ran in any of the dozen revisions they survived.
A vestigial remnant is the shrunken leftover of something formerly functional, and the sentence gives no history of function, only a record of being carried along unexecuted.
Spurious suggests something counterfeit or falsely introduced, but the lines were carried forward openly by the maintainers themselves through revision after revision.
The sentence never describes the lines as tangled or hard to follow; the only fact given about them is that control never reached them.
Missing comments would be a separate complaint, and the engineer's reason for deleting the lines is stated as their failure to execute, not the absence of explanation.
Erratic behavior implies the code runs unpredictably, which is ruled out by the statement that it never executed.
Ownership or licensing is nowhere at issue; the engineer is doing housekeeping on code that does nothing.
An engineer doing cleanup would not delete lines the program depended on, and code that never executes cannot be required for anything.
The sentence's whole justification for deletion is that the lines had never done anything across a dozen revisions.
Praise for the craftsmanship of the code would make no sense as a reason for removing it during a cleanup.

sentenceSets.sentence: Arguing about the seating chart after the last guest had gone home struck her as an otiose exercise, and she said so.

answerChoices.reasoning: Belated fixes on the lateness of the argument, but a late complaint can still change something; here the guests have already gone, so nothing the argument settles can affect the evening at all.
Gratuitous means uncalled for or unprovoked, yet the seating chart was a real arrangement that really happened, so the argument has a genuine subject and fails only because the occasion is over.
A quixotic effort chases a noble but unreachable ideal, and squabbling over where people sat at a dinner carries no idealism for the sentence to point to.
Fatuous locates the fault in the silliness of the arguers' reasoning, while the sentence locates it in timing: the last guest had already left.
The sentence reports her judgment of the argument rather than the mood of the people having it, and she objects to the exercise itself, not to anyone's irritability.
Nothing suggests the argument breached decorum in front of anyone; by the time it starts there is no audience left to offend.
Tedium is about how the argument felt to sit through, but she objects immediately and on principle, before any length has accumulated.
The seating chart was an actual arrangement at an actual dinner, so the dispute is about something real rather than an imagined case.
An argument that begins only after everyone has gone home cannot be pressing, and she objects to having it at all.
She speaks up against the argument, which makes no sense if she regarded it as yielding something worth having.
Praising the argument as well mannered would give her no reason to say so disapprovingly.
